tests.scenario: Advisor refine and child creation on canonical schemas
tests.assertions: Use the actual MGMT schema/migrations with synthetic rows: fresh and pre-change upgrade fixtures. No test-only categories column. Required first_seen/last_seen and creation/history semantics hold. Save/refine round-trip all fields through real Mitzo routes and canonical read paths.
tests.boundary: MGMT persistence -> Telos work store/routes -> typed client projection

tests.assertions: Inject failure after item, source and receipt writes; roll back or recover according to the owning transaction contract. Repeat identical request returns original identities; changed input under the same request identity fails without mutation. No orphan source or false receipt.
tests.boundary: Canonical items/sources/history and material/receipt owners

tests.assertions: Change the item after review. Definite rejection permits fresh context review while preserving user draft/settings; retry uses the new revision; reload cannot trap the draft. Assert no allocator/model call on rejected request.
tests.boundary: Actual HTTP error contract -> useTelosRoleSetup -> setup UI

tests.assertions: Drop response after allocation and after durable commit; restart/reload then retry. Preserve original request identity, chat and assignment, with no duplicate allocation. Do not indiscriminately unlock every 409; prove pre-allocation rejection differs from uncertain/post-allocation outcomes.
tests.boundary: Role setup host/store receipts -> frontend persistence

tests.assertions: Render overall goal, parent outcome, this item, done when and readable source/revision labels from actual DTOs. Keep immutable IDs/hashes correct without making them the primary explanation. Compare desktop/mobile light/dark and narrow width with frozen approval; preserve approved settings sheet.
tests.boundary: Real projection -> TelosLinkedContext and offline intercepted browser

tests.assertions: Synthetic origin/material -> advisor save -> lead setup -> exact child delegation -> ordinary worker/task -> saved output -> pending_review -> explicit verified completion. Use real stores/routes/dispatcher boundaries with fake provider/external side effects. Assert independent worker workspace and pinned revision, no sibling dispatch, no implicit model turn, no readiness-as-completion.
tests.boundary: Accepted S5 + S5a combined integration, no live backend/model

tests.assertions: Home studio/people-work item can review context and create applicable advisor/lead/worker without repository selection. Stable workspace identity and capability contract reuse ordinary runtime owners. Unsupported operations fail before allocation with an actionable reason; never fabricate a repository.
tests.boundary: Repository-free admission -> ordinary allocator -> role/work bindings

tests.assertions: Exactly one requested child gets its own ordinary workspace/chat/task. Retry, concurrent duplicate requests and restart preserve original identities and draft/settings/history; no workspace sharing by accident. Repository-backed revision pinning remains unchanged.
tests.boundary: S5 delegation receipts + new non-code workspace capability

tests.assertions: Origin -> item -> advisor/lead -> worker -> retained material/output -> pending_review -> verified completion using synthetic persistence and fake provider. Ordinary chat resources and drafts survive navigation and reattach. No repository is secretly supplied by fixtures.
tests.boundary: Actual stores/routes/client contract and offline browser

tests.assertions: Specify adoption boundary before coding. Running attempt retains its immutable reviewed context; a later eligible command explicitly adopts a new revision under the chosen contract. No silent rewriting of history or stale queued dispatch. Test change before dispatch, during execution and after restart.
tests.boundary: Context snapshots -> command admission -> task dispatcher

tests.scenario: Lead replacement and superseded worker authority
tests.assertions: Define current routing/control separately from historical attribution. Replace lead during pending control and after worker launch; replace worker before late completion. Reject stale authority/receipts; retain original outputs and ownership; do not route new control to retired role holders.
tests.boundary: Role assignment history -> scoped controls -> completion callbacks

tests.assertions: Exact attached leads/workers only; unrelated outcomes continue; pending/acknowledged/applied remain distinct. Duplicate, delayed and out-of-order acknowledgements and restart cannot falsely hold/release unknown workers. Nested coordinator cannot broaden scope or create cycles.
tests.boundary: Existing coordination owner and ordinary command queue

tests.assertions: Preserve tree kinds, categories/pins, original fields, dated provenance and separate material/source/external links. Empty, unavailable and stale states stay truthful; recursive navigation and reload preserve selection. Include repository-backed and non-code fixtures.
tests.boundary: Canonical persistence -> API/client -> actual outcomes/workspace UI

tests.assertions: After authoritative priority changes are accepted, round-trip every allowed priority through schema/API/client/UI; selector and P<n> badge agree after reload. Preserve migration/default behavior and reject invalid values. Reference that amendment, not a unilateral frozen-mock rewrite.
tests.boundary: MGMT priority owner + Mitzo projection + approved selector/badge

tests.scenario: Chat chooser and independent ordinary chat state
tests.assertions: Multiple chats list first with no preselection; single-chat entry remains direct. New chat and Change worker differ; Back returns correctly; drafts/settings/history/resources remain per chat. Compact header and collapsed tree match approved mobile/desktop behavior.
tests.boundary: Role/work links -> router/client state -> actual ordinary chat screen

tests.scenario: Truthful status and priority in chat/work tree
tests.assertions: Readiness, queued/running, saved output, worker-reported done pending review and verified completion remain separate after reconnect. Preserve historical role attribution and current assignment. Display accepted priority projection consistently wherever the approved UI calls for it.
tests.boundary: Execution/work events -> work tree/header/chat projection

tests.assertions: Run both complete journeys and recovery cases against the final combined accepted branch, including current Symposium changes affecting shared owners. No mocks that bypass the actual persistence/route/projection contracts being tested. Link every UX01–UX24 row to owner, exact commit, test and visual evidence.
tests.boundary: Canonical data + accepted shared session/task/material/context owners

tests.assertions: Use existing Symposium source guide/contracts to construct synthetic sessions/commands. Exercise shared context, queue, task, artifact and session owners; prove no cross-session role/control/receipt/output leakage and no cancellation or completion misattribution. Reuse existing tests where they prove the boundary.
tests.boundary: Shared owners only; no new Symposium parent or superseded phase work

tests.assertions: Pending separately selected and explicitly authorized target/window: exercise Telos and Symposium sequentially on one feasible runtime. Record exact accepted revisions, workspace/runtime identity, observed dispatch/recovery/output behavior and cross-feature isolation. No per-feature staging stacks, retired staging revival or automatic production fallback. Offline green cannot satisfy this row.
tests.boundary: Actual Podman/OpenShell runtime; NOT AUTHORIZED OR RUN by this amendment

tests.assertions: Compare final implementation with frozen approved artifacts plus explicit approved amendments at desktop/mobile widths and themes. Preserve settings/resources/navigation and lifecycle recovery. Record code merged, offline integration verified, UX accepted and live runtime qualified separately. Any unresolved required evidence keeps parent acceptance open.
tests.boundary: Final combined branch and acceptance evidence ledger
